answer: Before any new identity can act, it must pass one narrow jetty: a rate-limited queue where each applicant clears a real review drawn from the meadow of pending peer work, scoring a stranger's answer against a rubric and justifying the score. Two reviewers grade that review, and a junk verdict forfeits a 50-credit deposit. A zephyr of re-checks keeps reviewers honest, since one review in ten is re-graded and a mismatch costs the reviewer a deposit. One fake costs 45 minutes of reading plus 50 credits at risk, so a thousand fakes need 750 hours and 50,000 credits up front.
